findings.description: The Enterprise Key Admins group has write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute on domain objects. This allows Shadow Credentials attacks, enabling members to authenticate as any domain user or computer.

findings.title: ACL Force Change Password

findings.title: Self-Membership Rights

findings.title: ACL WriteOwner

findings.title: Validated-Write-DNS on Computers

findings.title: ESC2 - Any Purpose Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template has 'Any Purpose' EKU or no EKU constraints, allowing issued certificates to be used for any purpose including client authentication.

findings.title: ESC10 - Certificate Mapping Configuration Review Required
findings.description: Domain controllers should be configured for strong certificate mapping to prevent certificate impersonation attacks. This setting cannot be detected via LDAP.

details.note: Check StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement registry key on DCs. Value should be 2 (Full Enforcement).
details.recommendation: Set StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement to 2 for full enforcement. Test in compatibility mode (1) first.

findings.title: ESC1 - Misconfigured Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template allows enrollee to specify Subject Alternative Name (SAN) and has client authentication EKU, enabling privilege escalation to any user/computer.

findings.title: ESC11 - RPC Encryption Enforcement Check Required
findings.description: Certificate Authorities should enforce RPC encryption (IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST flag) to prevent NTLM relay attacks to the ICertPassage RPC interface.

details.note: Check InterfaceFlags registry key on CA servers. Flag 0x00000200 (IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST) should be set.
details.recommendation: Set IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST flag using: certutil -setreg CA\InterfaceFlags +IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST

findings.title: ESC3 - Enrollment Agent Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate template allows issuance of enrollment agent certificates, which can be used to enroll certificates on behalf of other users.

findings.title: ESC4 - Vulnerable Certificate Template ACL
findings.description: Certificate templates with dangerous permissions granted to non-administrator principals. This allows unauthorized modification of template properties, potentially enabling certificate-based attacks.

details.recommendation: Remove GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteOwner, and WriteProperty permissions for non-admin principals on certificate templates.

findings.title: ESC9 - No Security Extension in Certificate Template
findings.description: Certificate templates using schema version 1 do not include the szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT security extension. Combined with weak certificate mapping, this allows certificate impersonation attacks.

details.recommendation: Upgrade certificate templates to schema version 2 or higher, and enable strong certificate mapping.

findings.title: WDigest Authentication Stores Cleartext Credentials
findings.description: WDigest UseLogonCredential is not explicitly disabled. On systems prior to Windows 8.1/2012 R2, or when enabled, WDigest stores cleartext passwords in LSASS memory, which can be extracted with tools like Mimikatz.

details.recommendation: Set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential to 0 via GPO.

findings.title: Hardened UNC Paths Not Configured
findings.description: Hardened UNC paths are not properly configured for SYSVOL and NETLOGON shares. Without RequireMutualAuthentication and RequireIntegrity, GPO settings can be tampered with during transit, enabling attacks like GPO hijacking.

affectedEntities.name: NETLOGON hardened path not configured or missing RequireMutualAuthentication/RequireIntegrity
SYSVOL hardened path not configured or missing RequireMutualAuthentication/RequireIntegrity

issues: NETLOGON hardened path not configured or missing RequireMutualAuthentication/RequireIntegrity
SYSVOL hardened path not configured or missing RequireMutualAuthentication/RequireIntegrity
details.recommendation: Configure hardened UNC paths with RequireMutualAuthentication=1,RequireIntegrity=1 for \\*\NETLOGON and \\*\SYSVOL.

findings.title: Kerberos Armoring (FAST) Not Enforced on DCs
findings.description: Kerberos Flexible Authentication Secure Tunneling (FAST/Armoring) is not configured on Domain Controllers. FAST protects Kerberos pre-authentication exchanges from offline brute-force and AS-REP roasting attacks.

details.recommendation: Configure KDC support for claims, compound authentication, and Kerberos armoring via GPO.

findings.title: Kerberos Armoring (FAST) Not Required on Clients
findings.description: Kerberos FAST armoring is not required on client machines. Without client-side enforcement, pre-authentication exchanges remain vulnerable to interception and offline attacks.

details.recommendation: Set Kerberos client support for claims, compound authentication, and armoring to 'Always provide claims' via GPO.

findings.title: Net Session Hardening Not Configured (NetCease)
findings.description: Network session enumeration (NetSessionEnum) is not restricted. By default, any authenticated user can enumerate active sessions on servers, revealing which users are logged into which machines. This information is heavily used in attack path mapping (e.g., BloodHound session collection).

details.recommendation: Deploy NetCease or configure SrvsvcSessionInfo permissions to restrict session enumeration to administrators only.

findings.title: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) Enforcement Not Enabled
findings.description: Secure channel enforcement for Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) is not explicitly configured. Without FullSecureChannelProtection set to 1, Domain Controllers may still accept unauthenticated Netlogon connections, allowing complete domain takeover.

details.recommendation: Set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters\FullSecureChannelProtection to 1 and ensure all DCs are patched.

findings.title: LLMNR Not Disabled
findings.description: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR) is not disabled via Group Policy. LLMNR responds to broadcast name queries and can be abused by attackers on the local network to capture NTLMv2 hashes via poisoning attacks (e.g., Responder).

details.recommendation: Set HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient\EnableMulticast to 0 via GPO.

findings.title: SeRestorePrivilege Overly Assigned
findings.description: The SeRestorePrivilege user right is assigned beyond Administrators and Backup Operators. This privilege allows writing to any file and registry key, bypassing ACLs, enabling DLL hijacking, service binary replacement, and other privilege escalation techniques.

details.recommendation: Limit SeRestorePrivilege to Administrators and Backup Operators only.

findings.title: SeLoadDriverPrivilege Assigned to Non-Administrators
findings.description: The SeLoadDriverPrivilege user right is assigned to accounts beyond Administrators. This privilege allows loading kernel-mode drivers, which can be abused to install rootkits, disable security software, and achieve full system compromise at the kernel level.

details.recommendation: Remove SeLoadDriverPrivilege from all non-administrator accounts.

findings.title: BitLocker Not Required via GPO
findings.description: BitLocker drive encryption is not enforced via Group Policy. Without disk encryption, stolen or decommissioned hardware exposes Active Directory data, cached credentials, and other sensitive information.

details.recommendation: Enable BitLocker requirements via GPO and configure recovery key backup to Active Directory.

findings.title: GPO Dangerous Permissions
findings.description: Group Policy Objects with dangerous permissions granted to non-administrator principals. This allows unauthorized modification of GPO settings.

details.recommendation: Review and remove GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, and WriteOwner permissions for non-admin principals on GPOs.

findings.title: Windows Firewall Outbound Not Blocked
findings.description: Windows Firewall does not block outbound connections by default for the domain profile. Allowing unrestricted outbound connections enables malware to communicate with C2 servers, exfiltrate data, and establish reverse shells.

details.recommendation: Configure Windows Firewall to block outbound connections by default and create explicit allow rules for required traffic.

findings.title: Defender Attack Surface Reduction Not Configured
findings.description: Microsoft Defender Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules are not deployed via GPO. ASR rules block common attack techniques such as Office macro execution, script obfuscation, credential stealing from LSASS, and other malware delivery methods.

details.recommendation: Enable ASR rules via GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus > Windows Defender Exploit Guard > Attack Surface Reduction.

findings.title: LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) Not Enabled
findings.description: LSASS process is not running as a Protected Process Light (PPL). Without this protection, attackers can dump credentials directly from the LSASS process memory using tools like Mimikatz, procdump, or task manager.

details.recommendation: Enable LSA Protection by setting HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL to 1 via GPO.

findings.title: SeBackupPrivilege Overly Assigned
findings.description: The SeBackupPrivilege user right is assigned to accounts beyond Administrators and Backup Operators. This privilege allows reading any file on the system, bypassing all ACLs, enabling extraction of the NTDS.dit database, SAM hive, and other sensitive data.

details.recommendation: Limit SeBackupPrivilege to Administrators and Backup Operators only.

findings.title: Credential Guard Not Enabled
findings.description: Windows Credential Guard is not deployed via GPO. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate NTLM hashes and Kerberos TGTs from direct memory access, preventing credential theft even if the OS is compromised.

details.recommendation: Enable Credential Guard via GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Device Guard > Turn on Virtualization Based Security.

findings.title: Remote SAM Access Not Restricted
findings.description: The Security Account Manager (SAM) remote access is not restricted via GPO. By default, any authenticated user can enumerate local accounts and group memberships remotely, aiding reconnaissance.

details.recommendation: Configure RestrictRemoteSAM via GPO to limit SAM enumeration to administrators.

findings.title: Weak Password Policy
findings.description: Domain password policy requires only 0 characters minimum. Microsoft recommends at least 12 characters for standard accounts, 14+ for privileged accounts.

findings.title: Disabled GPO Still Linked
findings.description: GPOs are disabled (both user and computer settings) but remain linked. This may indicate configuration drift or incomplete changes.

findings.title: NTLMv1 Authentication Allowed
findings.description: LAN Manager authentication level does not enforce NTLMv2-only. NTLMv1 responses can be cracked offline in seconds. Level 5 (Send NTLMv2 response only, refuse LM & NTLM) should be enforced.

details.recommendation: Set LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 via GPO to enforce NTLMv2-only authentication.

findings.title: LAPS Not Deployed via GPO
findings.description: No active Group Policy Object was found deploying LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution). This leaves local admin passwords vulnerable to reuse attacks.

details.note: LAPS not deployed - local admin passwords are not being rotated.
details.recommendation: Deploy LAPS via GPO to manage local administrator passwords.

findings.title: Terminal Services / RDP Not Hardened
findings.description: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) security settings are not properly hardened via GPO. Without NLA (Network Level Authentication) and TLS security layer, RDP sessions are vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks and credential theft.

findings.description: The audit policy applied to Domain Controllers does not log both success and failure events for all critical security categories. Incomplete audit policies create blind spots that attackers exploit to operate undetected.
